## Overview

This model describes the assigned-arm word-reading contrast with two mediators, letter-sound knowledge ($L$) and nonword off-floor status ($N > 0$). It is the nonword companion to [MED-075](../lrp-rli-med-075/), which uses blending as its second mediator.

The nonword leg uses a Bernoulli likelihood for off-floor status. It includes the baseline off-floor indicator. The letter-sound and word-reading legs use graded Beta-Binomial likelihoods. Every leg uses the common pre-exposure adjustment vector, including the outcome and mediator baselines, baseline vocabulary and the declared hearing, speech and memory terms. Read `resolved_run_plan` and `model_recipe.md` for the terms and rows actually fitted.

The chained model predicts nonword status conditional on post-letter-sound score. The calculation integrates nonword status conditional on each simulated letter-sound value.

## Interpretation

- The joint indirect component (`NIE_joint`) summarises the fitted decomposition through the two-mediator block. Its nonword component concerns binary off-floor status, not graded decoding skill.
- The $L \to N$ coefficient describes an adjusted same-wave association. A positive coefficient does not establish temporal order or show that letter sounds cause decoding.
- The separate path components depend on the chosen mediator order and decomposition assumptions. Report their intervals and floor limitations without assuming that a path must be small.

None of these components identifies a causal pathway. Latent ability and treatment-induced dose confounding remain. See [the common-adjustment decision](../../../notes/202608231500-mediation-585-remediation.md) and [the mediation limits](../../../METHODS.md#2-bayesian-statistical-models).
